key_insight: A symmetry-adapted single-orbital tight-binding model can reproduce the low-energy band structure and spin splitting of chiral 1D hybrid lead halide perovskites using only a few effective hopping terms.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compact, interpretable model for predicting band-edge electronic, spin, optical, and transport behavior in chiral perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Built a single-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian on four symmetry-related sites per primitive cell.
Included layer, in-plane sublattice, and spin degrees of freedom with separate parameter sets for conduction and valence bands.
Analyzed accidental vs symmetry-enforced degeneracies using screw eigenvalues and antiunitary operators.
evidence_signal: The model was validated by reproducing density-functional-theory band dispersions and quantitatively capturing spin splittings and spin-polarization patterns near the band edges.
watch_item: The model is designed for low-energy band-edge physics, so accuracy away from the fitted energy range or under structural/chemical changes may require reparameterization.
paper_title: Single-orbital tight-binding model for chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites
